column1: # The step list of the agent kit: the one data file. "kit plan", "kit step"
# and the tests read it, on Linux, macOS and Windows. Read
# docs/design/2026-11-01-agent-run-kit.md.
# Each line that does not start with "#" has 17 fields, separated by tabs.
# The first such line holds the names of the columns. A reader finds a
# column by its name, not by its place. "-" means no value.
#   name         The name of the step. "kit step NAME@BACKEND" runs it.
#   kind         probe, terminals, first-run, permission, new-chat, resume,
#                interrupt or real-session. "kit step" runs the script
#                probes/agent/steps/<kind>.sh (or .ps1). "kit plan" lists a
#                step only when its script exists.
#   agent        claude, codex, agy or cursor-agent, or "-" for no agent. "kit
#                plan" lists the step only when the agent is installed.
#   backends     A comma list of none, tmux, pty, conpty, psmux and operator.
#                "none": the step starts no session. "operator": the
#                operator starts the agent in a real terminal, and the kit
#                only watches.
#   os           A comma list of linux, macos and windows.
#   needs        none, operator, login or screen. "login": the step needs
#                the login of the operator, so it skips with "--home
#                throwaway". With "--home fixture" a login step of Codex,
#                Claude Code, agy or Cursor runs with a fake model.
#                "screen": the step can change the screen of
#                the operator, for example with a macOS dialog.
#   cost         none, or turns:N (N model turns on the plan of the login).
#   pre          The fixed answers to the screens that can come before the
#                idle screen, for example a trust question. Pairs
#                REGEX=>KEYS, separated by ";;". When a line of the screen
#                matches REGEX, the step sends KEYS (tmux key names,
#                separated by spaces). A pair is used again only while its
#                REGEX still matches and the screen did not change, 3 s
#                after the last use, 3 times at most: a key that comes too
#                early is lost.
#                Each REGEX matches the line with the cursor, so that a key
#                goes only to the option that the pair names. The step never
#                answers a terms page or a data opt-in: it stops and asks the
#                operator. From scenarios/claude/permission-dialog.sh,
#                scenarios/codex/approval.sh and scenarios/agy/agy.sh.
#   idle_regex   An ERE that matches a line of the idle screen.
#   busy_regex   An ERE that matches a line of the busy screen.
#   dialog_regex An ERE that matches a line of a dialog screen.
#                The screen is idle when a line matches idle_regex, and no
#                line matches busy_regex or dialog_regex. One ERE alone
#                cannot do this: the idle box of Codex also shows while it
#                works, and the box of Claude can show under a dialog.
#   prompt       The fixed text that the step sends. For "resume", the
#                arguments of the new start of the agent.
#   wait_regex   An ERE for the screen that the step waits for after the
#                prompt: the file write dialog for "permission", the busy
#                screen for "interrupt". For "new-chat" and "resume" it is
#                idle_regex, with the idle rule above.
#   answer       The keys that the step sends after the wait, as tmux names
#                them, separated by spaces: Escape, Enter, C-c, 1.
#   windows      The changes on Windows, as KEY=VALUE pairs separated by
#                ";". "send=Tab": the key that sends the prompt is Tab, not
#                Enter. Codex 0.164.0 on Windows sends a message with Tab
#                (aw, reported; not measured here). "no", "false" or "0":
#                the line is not for Windows, and the Windows kit hides it.
#                "-": no change.
#   measures     What the step measures, for a person.
#   facts        A comma list of the numbers of the facts that the step
#                checks.
# The regexes of claude, codex and agy agree with the states of the screens
# in corpus/; tools/agent-kit-tests/test-core-plan.sh checks this. The
# corpus has no idle, dialog or busy screen of the Cursor CLI. Its regexes
# come from fixture runs of Cursor CLI 2026.11.05-86047df (fact 78), not
# from corpus screens.
